title: The Man Who Lived in an Iron Lung for 70 Years
style: Stylized realistic 3D CGI animation still, high-end animated explainer look, Pixar-meets-realism, cinematic soft lighting, detailed skin, hair and fabric, expressive faces, shallow depth of field, no text, no letters, no gore, vertical 9:16 framing.

sections.name: The Man Who Lived in an Iron Lung for 70 Years

lines.prompt: A 1950s hospital ward with rows of large cylindrical iron lung machines, children's heads poking out, nurses walking between them

lines: In the 1950s, hospitals were filled with rows of giant metal tubes.

lines.prompt: Close-up of a young boy lying inside an iron lung, only his head sticking out, a mirror above him so he can see the room

lines: They were iron lungs. Polio could paralyse the muscles you breathe with, so the machine breathed for you.

lines.prompt: Cutaway view of an iron lung showing air pressure arrows pulling the boy's chest outward, blue technical glow

lines: It changed the air pressure around your body, pulling your chest open, then letting it fall.

lines.prompt: A young man in the 1950s inside an iron lung reading a book held on a stand above him, determined expression

lines: In 1952, a six year old boy called Paul Alexander was put inside one.

lines.prompt: An older man with grey hair inside an iron lung, smiling, a graduation cap and law books on a stand nearby

lines: He spent most of his life in it, but still became a lawyer, and wrote a book, typing with a stick held in his mouth.

lines.prompt: Two children getting a polio vaccine from a smiling nurse in a 1950s school, sunlight

lines: He lived in his iron lung for more than seventy years. Thanks to the polio vaccine, almost no one needs one now.
